title: Adaptive 3D Pocket reaches 2 tool radii past the stock side: a vise with no model is in reach

body:
## What changed

PR #2035 (merge commit `983f527bd`) changed the Adaptive strategy of the 3D Pocket operation. The tool disc now goes past the stock side. It cuts the stock ring from the air.

- Operation and strategy: 3D Pocket, `PocketStrategy::Adaptive`, whole model only (not shell, not rest roughing). See `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:846`.
- Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and each other strategy keep the old band (`r - OPEN_SLACK`).
- Reach constant: `ADAPTIVE_BAND_PER_R = 2.0` at `crates/motion/src/machining3d/open_side.rs:67`. The band is `2 * r + OPEN_SLACK` (`stock_band`, line 71). `OPEN_SLACK` is 0.01 mm (line 34).
- Default: the reach is always on for this strategy. It is a `pub const`, not an operation parameter. A user cannot change it.
- The planner reads a wider air band of `stock.offset(4.0 * r)` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs:84`.
- The reach applies on each level down to the bottom (review note 4).

## What a user sees today

- A tagged fixture box that meets the band in XY and stands above the operation bottom refuses the operation at generation. The message starts with `AIR_BAND_FIXTURE` (`crates/app/src/operation/open_side.rs:98`, function `air_band_refusal`). The machine table is skipped.
- A vise or clamp with no fixture model: no note, no warning and no refusal was found in the diff or on `origin/main`. The check reads only tagged fixture boxes (`air_band_refusal`, line 64).
- No check can see a vise that has no model. The PR body says the post gate is not changed. Whether the post gate or the simulation has another check for this case: not confirmed.
- The only notice is the changelog row of PR #2035. It says the tool goes up to 2 tool radii past the stock side.
- A collision with a modelled fixture is refused at generation. A collision with the part is held by the plan's own law. Both are outside the defect floor. This issue is a design question, not a defect.

## The open question

How does the product handle a vise that has no model when the tool goes 2 tool radii past the stock side? Options:

1. Keep the reach as it is. Rely on the changelog row and on the fixture refusal.
2. Make the reach a user parameter of the operation, with a default. The default can be off or on.
3. Limit the reach when no fixture model exists in the document. For example, use the old band of `r - OPEN_SLACK` then.
4. Show a warning when the reach is used and no fixture model exists.

Options 2 to 4 can combine. The maintainer decides. Related issue: #339 (Handle fixtures/vises). This issue is not a duplicate of #339. #339 asks for fixture modelling. This issue asks what the operation does while no model exists.

Done means: the maintainer picks an option and the work is filed or done.

## Source

- PR #2035, merge commit `983f527bd`, issue #1950.
- Review comment, note 4: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2035#issuecomment-6972199583
- Review note 4 recommends an operation parameter for the band (default off, or default on with a clear warning). It calls this a design choice, not a defect.
- Files read on `origin/main`: `crates/motion/src/machining3d/open_side.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/open_side.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs`.
